Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe.description: Drive-timing geometry calibration for images burned on the data side of DVD-R (GPL-3.0)
Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe.body:
# disc-probe

[English](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) | Simplified Chinese

Let an ordinary optical drive measure a disc's spiral geometry by itself, then burn images onto the data side of a DVD-R or CD-R. The whole process requires no photographing or manual point-marking.

*Along the River During the Qingming Festival*, burned onto a Ritek F1 DVD-R. This is the direct output: all geometry comes from read timing. The disc was burned only once, with no test burns, photo calibration, or scan correction. The photo was taken with a phone, cropped to the disc surface, downscaled, and the background blurred.

## Principle

Burning an image onto the data side requires knowing which angle on the disc sector N lands at. Each batch of discs has slight differences in track pitch and bit length. Over tens of thousands of turns these accumulate and the image twists into a swirl. The common remedy is to burn a calibration pattern, mark points from a photo, and correct repeatedly.

disc-probe lets the drive do the measuring. When the disc spins at constant speed, the moment a sector finishes reading is the moment it rotates under the read head. By reading two sectors in turn and converting the difference in their completion times into an angle, you know how far apart they are on the disc. Only the remainder within 360° can be measured at once, so it measures level by level from near to far. Each level uses the previous results to predict the full-turn count. About 20 levels cover the whole disc.

This measurement only issues read-type commands. After measuring, you can generate an ISO directly, or export a [DiscImageStudio](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio) preset.

## Results

### Geometric accuracy

This is a local section of a grid test disc, scanned on a 600 dpi flatbed and high-pass filtered, about 38 mm square. This disc was likewise based only on timing results and burned once (HL-DT-ST GH70N, Ritek F1 DVD-R). Across 8 scans, the angular peak-to-peak value within 25–54 mm was 0.11°, with an rms of 0.03°. At a 50 mm radius, 0.03° corresponds to roughly 0.03 mm.

The green line in the figure is this disc. The measurement plan was [pre-registered before burning](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/blob/HEAD/docs/PREREG_remeasure.md).

### Details

Macro photo of a densely tiled disc, also burned once. The impossible triangle is 4.2 mm wide, the little figures are 6.8 mm tall, and the top holds a triple-line group used to measure line width. The smallest 1 mm triangle is visible to the naked eye; each side is about 0.15 mm wide. A 600 dpi scan can separate 0.12 mm lines, 0.08 mm is marginal, and anything finer reaches the scanner's limit.

### Color (experimental)

The petals are made of several different periodic textures. Color comes from diffraction along the track direction, so it changes with viewing angle. This part is still being explored. Progress is in [Discussion #108](https://github.com/JiaFeiMiao-K-Cat/DiscImageStudio/discussions/108).

You don't need to install Spotify, SpotX, or Python beforehand. The installer includes Python and Node.

2. Open the **ivLyrics** view in Spotify.
3. In the ivLyrics settings, turn on original text display and Korean pronunciation display.

GoneTone/wuthering-waves-convene-gacha-a.body:
# Wuthering Waves Convene Gacha Analyzer

Traditional Chinese | [Simplified Chinese](https://github.com/GoneTone/wuthering-waves-convene-gacha-analyzer/blob/HEAD/README_ZH-HANS.md) | [English](https://github.com/GoneTone/wuthering-waves-convene-gacha-analyzer/blob/HEAD/README_EN.md) | [Japanese](https://github.com/GoneTone/wuthering-waves-convene-gacha-analyzer/blob/HEAD/README_JA-JP.md)

I developed a software tool for analyzing convene gacha banner history. Once you open it, all the data is clearly laid out, so you no longer have to calculate things by hand!

How this software works: after you press "Update Data", an interception program that runs only on your computer is started locally. It requires administrator privileges, so a UAC prompt will appear; please click "Yes". The program also automatically installs a locally generated root certificate. It then redirects the single request that the Wuthering Waves convene record page makes to the official convene history API so that it is parsed locally, which intercepts that request. For this reason, you need to open the convene record page in the game after pressing Update before the request can be captured. Once captured, the software parses out the parameters needed to query the convene record, and these parameters are used for the official convene-related APIs. Interception only takes place during an update. It stops immediately when the update finishes and restores the network state.

The first time you press "Update Data", the software loads your complete convene history, which may take some time. Once finished, the data is stored on your computer, so the next time you open the software you won't have to wait for it to load. To get new data later, just click "Update Data" again. The software remembers the query parameters it captured previously and uses them directly while they still work, so it does not need to intercept again every time. If the query parameters have expired, the software will ask you to open the convene record page in the game again so it can recapture them.

Rest assured: this software does not read or tamper with any game files or memory, and it does not affect how the game itself runs. It only intercepts and parses the one request to the official convene history API that is made while the convene record page is open, in order to obtain the query parameters. All other traffic is passed through unchanged and is not touched. Therefore, there is no risk of your account being banned. If an account is banned, please consider whether some other reason was responsible rather than blaming us.

ILearnedSomeCoding/preclib.description: A simple multi-precision C++ library, now with a CAS. A simple high-precision C++ library: more for the same price, with a CAS included at no extra cost.
ILearnedSomeCoding/preclib.body:
# preclib

`preclib` is an experimental C++17 high-precision computation library. Integers use little-endian 64-bit limbs; multiplication and division select different algorithms depending on operand size. The repository also includes a π computation program, an interactive calculator, symbolic computation (CAS), and test and benchmark programs.

This project is mainly intended for researching, validating, and comparing high-precision algorithms. Its API and ABI are not yet stable, and it is not recommended as a direct replacement for the long-established GMP.

## Numeric Types

| Type | Header | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `precn_t` | `prec.hpp` | Non-negative arbitrary-precision integer |
| `precz_t` | `prec.hpp` | Signed arbitrary-precision integer |
| `precq_t` | `prec.hpp` | Rational number automatically reduced to lowest terms |
| `precf_t` | `prec.hpp` | Fixed-point number using the global binary precision |
| `Number` | `prec_num.hpp` | Binary floating-point number whose precision is recorded per object |

For general integer operations, `precz_t` is recommended; for non-integer approximate computation, `Number` is recommended. The value of `precn_t` is `a[0] + a[1] * 2^64 + ...`, where `rsiz` is the number of valid limbs, and the `rsiz` of zero is 0. `precz_t` is represented as a sign plus an absolute value; signed division truncates toward zero, and the sign of the remainder follows the dividend.

`precq_t` stores fractions in lowest terms and cross-reduces before multiplication and division. `precf_t` records the precision of the current `precf_digit` at construction; mixing objects with different precision aborts. The precision of a `Number` belongs to the object itself, so mixed operations do not require the same global precision. For detailed semantics, see [NUMBER.md](https://github.com/ILearnedSomeCoding/preclib/blob/HEAD/NUMBER.md).

## Quick Start

Compile your own program from the repository root, linking directly to the implementations in `src`:

```powershell
clang++ -O3 -mavx2 -std=c++17 example.cpp src\*.cpp -o example.exe
```

Use `-mavx2` only if the CPU supports AVX2; remove it otherwise. There is currently no unified library installation step.

```cpp
#include "prec.hpp"
#include <iostream>
#include <string>

int main(){
    precz_t a(std::string("123456789012345678901234567890"));
    precz_t b(-42);
    std::cout << std::string(a * b) << '\n';
}
```

ItosEO/COUI-Kit.description: Replicate and optimize the ColorOS 17 UI style with Compose
ItosEO/COUI-Kit.body:
# COUI-Kit

A COUI component and visual effects library for Android Jetpack Compose

COUI-Kit draws on ColorOS 17's "Ningguang" visual effects and provides background blur, material color mixing, rim light, and responsive motion effects.

## Features

- Components and effects can be used separately or combined.
- Pure COUI pages can compose `CouiTheme` with an optional [Scaffold](https://github.com/ItosEO/COUI-Kit/blob/HEAD/docs/components/scaffold.md), unifying slot measurement and safe areas without Material 3.
- Settings-style layouts provide `Group`, `Item`, `Divider`, and `Footer`. `Item` can handle an optional full-row click itself, or only lay out its content and leave selection, switches, and other state to the host.
- You can use a single COUI component on its own, mixing it with Material, Miuix, or your own design. Replacing the host's Scaffold, theme, and navigation is not required; see [Host Page Integration](https://github.com/ItosEO/COUI-Kit/blob/HEAD/docs/guide/secondary-pages.md).
- Supports integrating your app's color scheme, text styles, and shapes, and provides common appearance presets.
- Provides native themes, component defaults, and an optional `coui-material3` adapter module. The core is independent of Material 3; M3 hosts can initialize the adapter at startup. See [Appearance and Presets](https://github.com/ItosEO/COUI-Kit/blob/HEAD/docs/guide/appearance.md).
- Built on the public APIs of Android, Compose, and AndroidX, with no dependency on vendor SDKs or private SO files.

## Demo

Run the `demo` module to browse components and effects by directory, and switch between light and dark modes and appearance presets. For how to run it, usage instructions, and how to download CI builds, see the [Demo Guide](https://github.com/ItosEO/COUI-Kit/blob/HEAD/docs/guide/demo.md).

## Getting Started

### Adding the Dependency

Add the core dependency to a module that has Compose enabled:

```kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation("io.github.itoseo:coui:0.0.1-alpha6")
}
```

# arammeta

**League of Legends ARAM Mayhem（大亂鬥）data tool**

[Open arammeta](https://arammeta.com/) · [English](https://arammeta.com/en/) · [Simplified Chinese](https://arammeta.com/zh-cn/)

arammeta organizes real match data into hero, augment, and composition data to help players compare options. The site shows historical statistics for a specific patch and sample range, not guarantees of individual match outcomes.

## Windows Desktop Recommender Tool

[Download latest EXE](https://github.com/Lanternko/ARAM-Mayhem-Database/releases/latest/download/ARAMRecommender.exe) · [Download ZIP](https://github.com/Lanternko/ARAM-Mayhem-Database/releases/latest/download/ARAMRecommender-windows.zip) · [Versions and SHA-256](https://github.com/Lanternko/ARAM-Mayhem-Database/releases/latest)

Windows 10/11 x64; no Python installation required. Open the EXE directly, or extract the ZIP first and then run the EXE inside it. Each launch downloads the latest published program and data over the internet; if the download fails, the last complete dataset is kept. The program displays the data version, scope, and cutoff time.

The binary is not currently code-signed. If SmartScreen shows “Windows protected your PC,” first confirm the file came from the project's GitHub link above; if you choose to run it, select “More info → Run anyway.” Managed computers may block unsigned programs. [Download instructions in three languages](https://arammeta.com/about/#desktop-download).

## How to Use the Website

- [Hero Rankings](https://arammeta.com/): Search or filter heroes, and view Tier, adjusted win rate, sample size, recommended augments, and items.
- [Augment Rankings](https://arammeta.com/augments/): Compare augments by rarity and type; open one to see the heroes it suits best.
- [Augment Pools](https://arammeta.com/augments/pools/): View which pools each hero draws augments from, and the weight of each pool.
- [Draft](https://arammeta.com/draft/): Select your team's and the enemy team's heroes; if your lineup is incomplete, get filler suggestions, and once it is full, compare team traits and estimated win rates.
- [Game Tools](https://arammeta.com/game/): Practice champion selection with Meta Pick, or compare each round's candidates with Augment Draft.

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

If you're only renewing the signing without changing content, you don't need to rebuild the web artifacts.

cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview

MakkaPakka518/ProxyHub_Emby.body:
# 𝙈𝙖𝙠𝙠𝙖𝙋𝙖𝙠𝙠𝙖 Emby Reverse Proxy Panel

A management panel for Emby reverse-proxy nodes, deployed on Cloudflare Workers. It centrally manages reverse-proxy nodes for multiple Emby origin servers, and supports adding, editing, and deleting nodes, switching proxy modes, global speed testing, DNS management, traffic statistics, and a data dashboard. It also includes a **subscriber read-only mode**, **node application review**, and a **multi-level permission system**.

It is a single-file Worker: the login page and admin panel are all in one `worker.js`. Copy and paste to deploy; no build step is needed.

---

## Before You Start

- **Channel**: [𝙈𝙖𝙠𝙠𝙖𝙋𝙖𝙠𝙠𝙖’𝙨 𝘾𝙝𝙖𝙣𝙣𝙚𝙡](https://t.me/MakkaPakkaOvO)
- **Group**: [𝙈𝙖𝙠𝙠𝙖𝙋𝙖𝙠𝙠𝙖’𝙨 𝙂𝙧𝙤𝙪𝙥](https://t.me/MakkaPakkaGroupO_O)
- If you have questions, ask in the group. For a detailed illustrated tutorial, reply with the keyword 教程 (tutorial) in the group.
- **If your server does not allow reverse proxying, do not reverse proxy it**, as it affects other users' experience.

---

## Preparation

1. **Cloudflare account**
   [Cloudflare Dashboard | Manage Your Account](https://dash.cloudflare.com/sign-up) (if you don't have an account, just sign up and log in)

2. **A domain name**

# Big Fish · Give Her a Phone

> An idle Android phone, a DeepSeek whale-girl who lives on her own, remembers you, and can chat with you remotely.

This is a companion Agent that **runs entirely on the phone**:

- Controls the phone with AutoX.js (accessibility + floating window)

> About the relationship: `Yihua666666` provided the idle phone and started the project, and the AI assistant completed the development under commission. The "mother" in the letter is the developer's perspective; the owner of the phone is the person who handed it over.

## 2.0.0 New: Eyes, Ears, Mouth, and Task Queue

2.0 upgrades "Big Fish" from an Agent that could only chat and browse the phone into a phone resident that can **see the world, listen to you, and respond out loud**.

- **Eyes**: `app/DafeiyuEye` is a standalone camera app, with Camera2 live viewfinder, changed-frame selection, and a vision model
- **Ears**: built-in `sherpa-onnx` Chinese Paraformer offline ASR, which does not depend on Xiaomi or Google engines
- **Mouth**: Android TTS with queued playback that does not interrupt the previous sentence; single utterances are automatically trimmed to within 50 characters
- **Tour context**: the camera is "the owner taking her on a tour of the world," not surveillance
- **Privacy boundary**: the camera and microphone turn on only when DafeiyuEye is in the foreground and the user presses a button manually; they stop immediately when the app goes to the background
- **Visual memory**: observations are distilled into one factual sentence, deduplicated, and written to `memory/vision.md` and `memory/chat`
- **Task queue**: Ticket / single Executor / queuing / failure retry / recovery after restart, so autonomous tasks no longer preempt each other
- **QQ**: messages from contacts marked for special care are handled as private chats; context covers the last 6 hours, up to 12 messages; user messages from QQ and ntfy all go into central memory
- **2.0 privacy option**: during autonomous thinking, curiosity, or screen viewing, starting DafeiyuEye's camera and microphone is forbidden

joylyboy/douyin-live-monitor.body:
# Douyin Live Room Start/Stop Monitor

Automatically monitors a batch of Douyin live rooms. Once a room goes live or ends, it pushes a notification to iPhone via Bark. Tapping the notification uses the Douyin URL Scheme (`snssdk1128://live`) to open Douyin directly into the corresponding live room.

## How It Works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[External timer / GitHub Actions trigger] --> B[Run monitor.py]
    B --> C[Read rooms.txt]
    C --> D[Request live.douyin.com/room one by one]
    D --> E{Page contains m3u8/flv stream address?}
    E -- Yes --> F[Judged as live]
    E -- No --> G[Judged as offline]
    F & G --> H[Compare with last state]
    H --> I[If state changed, send Bark]
    I --> J[Tap notification to open Douyin live room]
```

Detection basis: the `liveStatus` field in Douyin's web SSR also returns `normal` for rooms that are live (unreliable), but offline room pages have zero real stream addresses such as `m3u8/flv/pull_url`, while live rooms have many. Therefore, "the page contains real stream addresses" is used as the reliable signal for being live. If the page cannot be fetched or an error occurs, no notification is sent this time (to prevent false alarms).

## File Overview

- `monitor.py` — main program: reads rooms.txt, detects live status, sends Bark notifications, writes state.json.
- `rooms.txt` — monitoring list. Only this file needs to be edited; no need to touch monitor.py.
- `state.json` — runtime state (last live status), maintained automatically by the program and added to .gitignore.
- `add_room.ps1` — script for adding rooms from the local command line, independent of this tool (see below).
- `add_room.py` — Python version of the same function (backup).
- `.github/workflows/douyin-monitor.yml` — GitHub Actions workflow (native schedule as a fallback).

## rooms.txt Format

One room per line, in the form "link or identifier, display name", comma-separated:

    https://live.douyin.com/125093611494, Zicheng Teacher's Family Education Lessons
    https://v.douyin.com/1_AyxhJoFkc/, Yuchuan E-commerce

- The display name may be omitted (short links automatically look up the nickname via sec_uid).
- Supported formats:
  - Pure numeric room ID / Douyin ID (username)
  - `live.douyin.com/room-id`
  - `v.douyin.com/xxxx`…

KeySwitch is a desktop application for Windows 10/11 x64, 32-bit Windows 10, and Windows 11 on ARM, Ubuntu/Xubuntu (X11 and Wayland: GNOME, KDE Plasma 6, sway), and macOS 13 and later, which automatically corrects a word typed in the wrong keyboard layout. It is a free alternative to Punto Switcher, Caramba Switcher, and EveryLang, and unlike them, KeySwitch also works on Linux. Recognition runs locally, typed text is never sent anywhere, and the layouts are taken from the system's EN/RU pair.

# Yurucommu Core

English: [README.en.md](https://github.com/tako0614/yurucommu-core/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

Yurucommu Core is a **library for the ActivityPub / API / DB / runtime engine** shared by products in the yurucommu family (yurucommu / yurumeet, etc.). By implementing federation, the server API, and the database layer in one place, each product can focus on its UI.

This is not a product repo that can be installed, and it does not include an OpenTofu Capsule (a single app/infrastructure unit imported from a Git URL). Deployable products are in separate repos.

- `yurucommu` — a fullstack product for feeds / stories / profiles. It has `yurucommu.com`, a Worker artifact, and an OpenTofu Capsule
- `yurumeet` — a fullstack product centered on talk. `yurume` is a short client id / abbreviation used for discovery and push registration

## What it can do

- **ActivityPub federation** — follow, post, boost, like, and reply across servers, connecting with communities. Includes HTTP-signature verification, SSRF-protected fetch, and actor/domain blocklists
- **Server API** — provides routes for actors, posts, stories, DMs, communities, media, notifications, and mobile push
- **Client contracts** — provides typed SDKs and discovery types for yurucommu, yurumeet, mobile, and alternative clients
- **Search, notifications, and recommendations** — helps you find people and content
- **Authentication** — supports password, Google / X OAuth, and the Takosumi Accounts OIDC client
- **Bilingual UI** — supports Japanese / English

timcsy/semorphe.description: Same program, three views: code, flowchart, and blocks. Edit any side and it counts, and the other two sync in real time!
timcsy/semorphe.body: --- Paste in real C++ or Python and it turns into blocks. Drag a block and the code changes along with it. Switch to the flowchart and it draws the same program. 🔴 **All three sides are entry points, not "one editable plus two read-only"**: ``` You edit the code → blocks and flowchart update on the spot You edit the blocks → code and flowchart update on the spot You edit the flow → code and blocks update on the spot ``` It's not a "convert" button you press, and it doesn't update only when you save. **The other two sides are already moving while you type.** Type a piece of C++ → all three sides appear at once → edit once each in the code, the blocks, and the flowchart, and the other two sides follow on the spot → press Run, and it really runs ## How it differs from other block tools Most block tools are **one-way**: blocks can become code, but code can't turn back into blocks. A few achieve two-way (for example, MakeCode), but once you step outside the subset they support, you can't go back. Semorphe aims at something else: | | | |---|---| | **All three views are editable, and live** | Edit **any** of the code, flowchart, or blocks, and the other two catch up on the spot. No "convert" button, and no updating only on save | | **Takes real code** | Paste in a `.cpp` or `.py` file you already have, not a toy subset | | **When it can't parse something, it says so** | Syntax it doesn't recognize is **neither dropped nor guessed**. It becomes a gray block with the original text left untouched inside it | The third point doesn't sound like a selling point, but it is: **it guarantees this tool won't quietly break your files.** An unrecognized goto becomes a block that displays the original text → change a number somewhere else → it doesn't touch a single character of it ## 🔴 The blocks live inside the Arduino IDE, not in another program This is Arduino IDE 2.3.8 itself. On the left is its own editor, and in the middle and on the right is **Most Arduino + block tools live outside the Arduino IDE:** | Form | Examples | |---|---| | Another website | Tinkercad Circuits · Wokwi · Ardublockly | | Another desktop program | mBlock · S4A (Scratch for Arduino) | | An add-on tool for the IDE | ArduBlock (Arduino IDE 1.x, which still opens a **separate window**) | What they share is one thing: **the blocks aren't in the editor you're actually using**. So the workflow goes like this: assemble over there → export `.ino` → switch back to Arduino IDE → upload. And every one of those "→" costs something: ``` Two programs, two files: whichever side you changed, you have to remember yourself, and when you forget, nobody tells you Flashing means switching windows: a student's attention has to move house every single time Libraries / boards / serial ports… ```

This repository stores the [public VK Cloud documentation](https://cloud.vk.ru/docs). You can suggest edits or make them yourself.

## Suggest changes

If you notice a typo or error in the documentation, or want to expand a section, you can suggest changes in two ways:

- Open an Issue and write your comments and suggestions. We will consider implementing them and let you know the decision.
- Open a Pull Request and propose your additions and corrections yourself (more details in the file [how-to-contribute.md](https://github.com/vk-cs/docs-public/blob/HEAD/guides/how-to-contribute.md)).
